text: For the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system with sech^2 soliton IC (v=2*sech^2(x+5), u=v^2/2+0.2v, perturbed from the Gardner reduction), does the soliton structure survive to T=8? Specifically: does final v retain a dominant peak with amplitude >= 1.0 (50% of initial 2.0), does mass(v) drift < 8%, and do both fields stay bounded?

method: Fourier pseudospectral spatial discretization (exact derivatives via FFT), explicit RK4 time integration, no dealiasing
bank_use_rationale: No bank available (NoKB). E1 is the minimal baseline: Fourier pseudospectral is natural for periodic-domain dispersive PDEs (exact spatial derivatives), explicit RK4 is the simplest standard time integrator. dt=1e-4 satisfies dispersive CFL: k_max^3 * dt = (2pi*128/30)^3 * 1e-4 ≈ 1.93 < 2.83 (RK4 imaginary-axis stability radius 2*sqrt(2)).

diagnostics.failure_mode: overflow in nonlinear multiply (u*ux, v*vx) followed by NaN in FFT — classic aliasing blow-up signature
diagnostics.note: u grew from ~2.4 to 6.5 by t=2, suggesting aliasing-driven energy accumulation in high-k modes

rationale: Simulation diverged before T=8. No-dealiasing pseudospectral is aliasing-unstable for these quadratic nonlinearities. Single fix needed: 2/3-rule (Orszag) dealiasing to zero top 1/3 modes in products.
F1 failure mode is aliasing blow-up (overflow in multiply, NaN in FFT). Single-component upgrade: add 2/3-rule dealiasing (zero modes |n| > Nx/3) to all nonlinear products. Everything else unchanged.

method: Fourier pseudospectral + explicit RK4 + 2/3-rule (Orszag) dealiasing — zero modes |n| > Nx/3 in all spectral products
bank_use_rationale: No bank (NoKB). F1 failure mode = aliasing overflow. 2/3 rule is the canonical single-component fix for quadratic-nonlinearity aliasing in pseudospectral methods. All other components identical to E1.

diagnostics.failure_mode: v field fragmented into 79 oscillatory peaks (scale ~3 grid pts) — Gibbs-type ringing at 2/3 hard cutoff. Hard spectral truncation causes cutoff-scale ringing; energy spuriously transfers from v to u. Soliton does not survive as coherent structure.

rationale: Run completed but v_max_final=0.68 < 1.0 (target). Root cause: hard 2/3 cutoff creates persistent cutoff-scale ringing in v (79 peaks at T=8). Need smooth spectral filter to damp high-k modes without inducing ringing.

F2 shows hard 2/3 cutoff causes Gibbs ringing at the cutoff scale (79 small peaks in v). Single-component upgrade: replace hard 2/3 cutoff with smooth Hou-Li exponential filter sigma(n)=exp(-36*(|n|/(Nx/2))^36), applied after each RK4 step. Tapers high-k modes smoothly, eliminating cutoff ringing while still suppressing aliasing.

method: Fourier pseudospectral + explicit RK4 + Hou-Li exponential spectral filter (sigma(n)=exp(-36*(|n|/128)^36)) applied after each RK4 step — replaces hard 2/3 cutoff from E2
bank_use_rationale: No bank (NoKB). F2 failure = cutoff ringing from hard 2/3 truncation. Hou-Li smooth exponential filter is the standard single-component fix: preserves low-k modes (soliton) while smoothly damping near-Nyquist modes that cause ringing.

diagnostics.failure_mode: Hou-Li filter applied at every step (80,000 times) is catastrophically over-dissipative: modes at eta=0.9 (n=115) decay as 0.444^80000 ~ 0. Soliton is killed by cumulative numerical dissipation.
diagnostics.note: Self-rollback to E3-refined (= E2 with full-spectrum linear v_xxx + 2/3 dealiasing for nonlinear terms only). This gives v_max=0.635, 9 peaks, one dominant (2.7x larger than second), mass drift 0%, all bounded. Better physical structure than E2 original (79 Gibbs peaks) even though peak amplitude slightly lower.

rationale: E3 over-dissipated. Self-rollback to refined E2 variant: full-spectrum linear v_xxx + 2/3 dealiasing on nonlinear products. Final result: v_max=0.635, 9 peaks (dominant at 0.635, next at 0.235), mass drift=0%, both fields bounded. Amplitude below 1.0 target — likely physical: epsilon=0.2 perturbation drives large m=u-v^2/2 growth (from 0.4 to 7.5), which back-reacts to drain v soliton.
